tool_summary: The Go toolchain. `go run` compiles and immediately executes source, `go build` compiles without executing, and `go get`/`go install` fetch and can execute build-time code (though Go's module system does not run arbitrary install scripts the way npm/gem do).
platform_notes: Behavior is consistent across Linux and macOS.

rules.description: Compiles and immediately executes the given package or source file. The source content is not inspected by commandant; whatever the program does, it does with the invoking user's privileges at run time.
rules.reversible_note: Reversibility depends entirely on what the compiled program does, which commandant does not inspect.

rules.description: Fetching a module from a non-standard proxy (GOPROXY override) or with GOFLAGS/GONOSUMCHECK-style checksum bypass reduces the supply-chain verification Go's module system otherwise provides.
rules.notes: This rule assumes a leading VAR=value prefix before the go binary is visible in the same raw command string commandant assesses. posix_parser.cr does not appear to have explicit handling for leading environment variable assignments (binary = tokens.first), so if such a prefix causes the parser to treat 'GOPROXY=...' itself as the binary/tool name rather than part of the go invocation, this rule would never be reached at all. This should be verified against actual parser behavior before relying on this rule.

rules.description: Fetches and builds a module. Go's module system does not execute arbitrary install-time scripts the way npm/gem do, but the fetched source will be compiled (and, for `go install`, its binary made available), and any `//go:generate` or build-constrained code can still run at build time.
Uses the Go toolchain. Subcommands not otherwise matched (build, test, vet, fmt) compile or analyze code without executing the resulting binary.
